فَوَلِّ وَجْهَكَ شَطْرَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ

“So turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram.” (Qur’an 2:144)

Qibla Direction Finder

Find the direction of the Kaaba in Makkah from wherever you are, measured from true north along the shortest path on the globe.

​
New York, United States

58.5°ENE

clockwise from true north

The Kaaba is 10,306.3 km (6,404 miles) away.

How to use it

  1. On a phone, lay it flat and away from metal, magnets and speakers.
  2. Calibrate the compass if asked: move the phone in a figure of eight.
  3. Turn yourself until the gold Kaaba on the dial points straight ahead.
  4. On a computer, use the degrees with any compass. The angle is from true north, not magnetic north.
  5. No compass? Check against a landmark: the sun sets roughly in the west.

Why does North America face north-east?

The Earth is round, so the shortest path to Makkah is a great circle. On a flat map Makkah looks south-east of New York, but the shortest path heads north-east, over the Atlantic. This is the method most scholars use today, and the one the Fiqh Council of North America has endorsed.

The Kaaba is at 21.4225° N, 39.8262° E. Small differences of a degree or two are well within what scholars accept when facing the Qibla.
